foundation.logline: A harbour ferry is designed with two identical working ends and sides that open along their whole length, so a crowd can board at once, and every stage of building it tests whether that open side can close into shelter.

design_thesis.central_idea: The ferry is one long covered hall with two identical working ends. Each side opens along almost its full length through a row of sliding gates, so passengers board across the width all at once and the vessel departs in whichever direction its next pier lies. Closed, each gate sits flush between two posts; opened, it slides toward one end along a track just outside the hull plating and stacks behind its neighbour, leaving the side clear from post to post.
design_thesis.visible_difference: The vessel reads as a low, even body with the same profile at both ends, one continuous roof, and a long band of gates along each side. A small glazed helm cabin sits on the roof at mid-length, facing both ends, reached from the hall by a crew stair beneath it.
design_thesis.spatial_consequence: Benches run across the hall from one side to the other, so every seat lies a few steps from a gate on each side. The hall is one undivided space between two open sides, and its width, not its length, joins the seats to the pier.
design_thesis.coherence: The identical ends, the side gates and the cross benches all serve one rule: people move on and off across the ferry's width. Each depends on the other two, and together they turn a stop into a single movement of the whole crowd.

principal_dimensions.rationale: Length is set by how much of a waiting crowd must reach a gate at the same moment, so the hull is long enough for a full pier queue to board side by side. Beam is set by the cross benches and the standing space inside each row of gates, and ends where those bands end.

space_plan.placement: The whole main deck between the two working ends, on the centreline, with a row of gates along the port side, another along the starboard side, and the helm cabin above it on the roof at mid-length.
space_plan.role: Passengers board here across the width, sit on the cross benches during the crossing and stand at the gates before each stop; the film's question is answered in this room.
space_plan.layout_decision: It fits the arrangement without a change: the hall is the ferry's one long room, and the benches run across it from gate row to gate row.

premise.question: Can a vessel that opens its whole side to the pier still feel like shelter once it is crossing open water?
premise.force: Every opening that makes boarding quick is also an opening for wind and spray once the ferry is under way.
premise.device: The film keeps returning to the row of side gates: drawn as a single line, framed in steel, hung and adjusted, and finally opened and closed by the crew at a pier.
premise.change: A row of gates argued over on paper becomes a routine the crew performs by habit, and passengers board together across the width.
premise.answer: The ending shows passengers crossing open water beside the closed side without looking up, and standing ready in front of the closed gates as the far pier comes alongside.

foundation.synopsis: An operator wants less of each crossing spent at the stops, and a design team answers with a ferry that has two identical working ends. Its hull is one long covered hall with a row of sliding gates along each side and benches running across its width, and a small helm cabin sits on the roof at mid-length above a crew stair. The argument is over the side: every opening that speeds boarding is also an opening for wind and spray once the ferry is under way. In the yard, the hull is built with matching ends and its sides are framed as rows of openings with posts between them. Fitting-out crews hang each gate and adjust it against its neighbours until a closed side reads as one surface, and the hull is coated while it still stands on its blocks in the building dock. The dock is flooded, the finished ferry floats off its blocks and is warped out through the dock gate into the harbour with both sides closed. In service, a waiting crowd steps aboard across the width in one movement, the gates close behind the last passenger, and the ferry pulls away in the direction it arrived from. Out on open water the passengers sit beside the closed side as spray strikes it, and at the far pier they are already standing at the gates before the ferry stops.

stage_treatments.dramatic_purpose: The film has to settle one decision before anything is made: whether the ferry can work from two identical ends so that people move on and off across its width.
stage_treatments.observable_development: The design team lays a row of card benches across a long strip of paper, marks gates along both edges and turns the strip end for end to show it reads the same either way. Operator representatives sweep a hand across the strip in one motion, from the pier edge to the benches. The helm cabin is slid along the roof of the model until it sits at mid-length, facing both ends, above the crew stair that reaches it from the hall.
stage_treatments.participants: The design team, with operator representatives who bring the question of every stop into the room.
stage_treatments.handover_to_next: The agreed arrangement leaves the studio as drawings of a hull with matching ends and open sides.

stage_treatments.dramatic_purpose: The idea has to become a hull, and its sides have to rise as rows of openings from the first framing.
stage_treatments.observable_development: Yard crews set out the framing for both ends from the same template, and site engineers hold one end's drawings against the other's steel. Along each side the structure rises as a row of openings with posts between them, and the roof goes on over the hall while the sides are still bare.
stage_treatments.participants: Yard crews and site engineers, working along the length of the same hull.
stage_treatments.handover_to_next: The framed hull, with its row of openings on each side, passes to the fitting-out crews.

stage_treatments.dramatic_purpose: This is where each open side has to become a wall that can close, so the gates have to be made to work as one surface.
stage_treatments.observable_development: With the hull still on its blocks in the building dock, fitting-out crews hang the gates one by one, sliding each shut against the one before it and adjusting its runners until the edges meet. The hull and the roof are coated, and the helm cabin is glazed toward both ends. A crew member walks the length of a closed side, running a hand along the seams.
stage_treatments.participants: Fitting-out crews, working gate by gate along both sides.
stage_treatments.handover_to_next: The coated ferry, with every gate hung and its hall fitted, stands finished on its blocks, ready to be floated out.

stage_treatments.dramatic_purpose: The finished ferry has to leave the yard as one coherent vessel, its closed sides reading as walls from the water.
stage_treatments.observable_development: Yard crews flood the building dock. The water rises along the closed sides until the coated, finished ferry lifts off its blocks and floats. The dock gate opens and the yard crews warp the ferry out into the harbour, its gates closed along both sides, while the master watches from the helm cabin at mid-length.
stage_treatments.participants: Yard crews, with the master aboard.
stage_treatments.handover_to_next: The ferry leaves the yard for its home pier and goes into service.

stage_treatments.dramatic_purpose: The film answers its opening question with ordinary passengers who board together and settle as if the crossing were a room.
stage_treatments.observable_development: At the home pier the master opens the gates along the pier side from the helm cabin, and a waiting crowd steps aboard across the width and spreads along the benches. When the last passenger is clear of the gate line the gates close, and the ferry pulls away in the direction it came from.
stage_treatments.handover_to_next: The film leaves the viewer with the side gates opening and closing as an ordinary part of every stop.

foundation.ending: The last moments stay with the crossing. Out on open water, spray strikes the closed gates along the windward side while the passengers who boarded together sit on the benches beside them, reading and talking. As the far pier comes alongside they stand and wait in front of the closed leaves, already where the opening will be. Whether an open side could still shelter people is answered by passengers who sit beside it in open water without looking up.

characters.name: The ferry
characters.description: A harbour ferry built as one long covered hall with two identical working ends, gates along both sides and benches across its width.
characters.appearance: A low, even body with the same profile at both ends, one continuous roof, and a long band of sliding gates along each side; a small glazed helm cabin sits on the roof at mid-length, above a crew stair.

profile.spatial_layout: One passenger hall fills the main deck between the two ends. Structurally the hall is one open span under the roof, carried by the posts along its port and starboard sides. Passengers board and leave through the gates on whichever side lies against the pier. The crew reach the crew spaces inside the hull and the helm cabin above the roof by one stair at mid-length, and walk along the hall to the mooring stations at both ends. Nothing divides the hall along its length.
profile.deck_organization: The main deck is the hall, level from end to end and a short step above the pier, with the cross benches and a clear standing band inside each row of gates. The crew spaces lie below it, inside the hull. The roof carries the helm cabin at mid-length, reached from the hall through the hatch in its floor, and, as a proposal, a narrow walkway around the cabin for cleaning its glazing; passengers never go up there.
profile.materials_and_finishes: All finishes here are proposals. A painted steel hull in a dark working colour, an aluminium roof in a lighter grey, and gate leaves framed in the hull colour with clear glazing in their upper halves. Benches are plain timber slats on steel frames.
profile.amenities: Benches run across the hall from the port row of gates to the starboard row, each within a few steps of a gate. As a proposal, racks for bicycles stand against the bulwark at both ends of the hall, where they do not block a gate.
profile.windows_and_glazing: The upper half of every gate leaf is glazed, so with the gates closed the port and starboard sides each read as a band of windows along the whole hall. The helm cabin is glazed on all four sides so it can see both ends over the roof.
profile.wellness_and_relaxation: The only place to rest is the hall itself. The closed gates keep the wind out while passengers sit on the benches beside them, with the harbour visible through the glazed upper halves.
profile.transformable_spaces: The port or the starboard side changes from a closed glazed wall to an open edge between slim posts when its gates slide toward one end. A waist-height rail folds up inside each opening while the ferry is underway and drops flat for boarding. With one side open at a pier, the whole hall is aired across its width.
profile.capacity: The hall seats a full pier queue at once and has standing room inside each row of gates. There are no cabins. A crew of three runs the ferry. The seated and crew figures are proposed; the standing figure is not decided.
profile.construction_new_build_and_refit: A new build. The steel hull is framed from one template used at both ends, each side is framed as a row of openings with posts between them, and the aluminium roof is lifted on after the gates are hung and adjusted.

signature_features.name: Full-length sliding side gates
signature_features.location: Along almost the whole length of the port and starboard sides of the main deck, between slim posts under the roof edge.
signature_features.visual_difference: A closed side reads as one continuous glazed wall; an open side leaves a clear run from pier to bench with no door frames.
signature_features.fixed_and_moving_parts: The posts and the upper and lower runner tracks are fixed; the gate leaves move.
signature_features.standard_geometry: Each leaf sits in its own opening, flush with the posts, so the port and starboard sides each read as one glazed wall from end to end under the roof edge.
signature_features.other_states: Open on one side: every leaf on that side has slid toward the same end over its neighbour into a stack behind a post; the other side stays closed.
signature_features.motion_and_clearance: The leaves unlatch together, slide along the outer track and stack behind their posts, inside a narrow band just outside the hull plating.
signature_features.access_and_furniture: Passengers step straight from the pier across the open side to the benches; the folding rail drops flat before boarding.
signature_features.verification: Weathertight seal of closed leaves in a seaway; locking of stacked leaves under wind load.

signature_features.name: Mid-length helm cabin facing both ends
signature_features.location: On the roof at mid-length, on the centreline, directly above the crew stair.
signature_features.visual_difference: A small glazed box stands alone in the middle of the long roof instead of a wheelhouse at one end, so the ferry has no front or back.
signature_features.standard_geometry: A low box standing on the roof at mid-length on the centreline, square in plan and glazed on all four sides, its floor a step above the roof and its flat top the highest point of the ferry. In profile it rises from the long roof line like a small lantern and looks the same from either end. A hatch in its floor opens over the crew stair.
signature_features.access_and_furniture: Reached from the hall by the crew stair at mid-length, which rises through the roof to the floor hatch; a door on its port side opens onto the roof walkway. One helm console faces each end.
signature_features.verification: Sight lines to both ends over the roof.

signature_features.name: Folding boarding rail inside each opening
signature_features.location: Inside every gate opening along the port and starboard sides, at the inner edge of the standing band.
signature_features.visual_difference: With the gates open the side still has a guard line while the ferry is underway, and nothing at all when it is boarding.
signature_features.fixed_and_moving_parts: The hinge brackets on each post are fixed; the rail sections fold.
signature_features.standard_geometry: A waist-height rail spans each opening between its posts, just inside the closed gate leaves, so from outside it shows only through the glazing.
signature_features.other_states: Lowered: each rail section folds down flat against the deck edge to leave the opening clear for boarding.
signature_features.motion_and_clearance: Each section swings down about its lower hinge into a recess in the deck edge; the standing band beside it must be clear.
signature_features.access_and_furniture: Raised underway beside the benches; lowered only while the ferry lies at a pier.
signature_features.verification: Holding load of a raised rail; trip risk of the recess when lowered.

interior_spaces.position: The whole main deck between the two working ends, on the centreline, with the port row of gates on one side, the starboard row on the other, the crew spaces below it inside the hull and the helm cabin above it on the roof at mid-length.
interior_spaces.layout: One long open room with nothing dividing it along its length. Cross benches run from the port standing band to the starboard one, each a few steps from a gate, with a clear standing band inside each row of gates. As a proposal, bicycle racks stand against the bulwark at both ends, clear of every gate.
interior_spaces.access: Passengers enter and leave through the gates on whichever side lies against the pier. The crew reach it from the crew spaces below and from the helm cabin by the crew stair at mid-length, and walk along it to the mooring stations at both ends.
interior_spaces.materials_and_light: As proposals, plain timber benches on steel frames, a painted steel floor and the underside of the aluminium roof left plain. Daylight comes through the glazed upper halves of the gate leaves along both sides; as a proposal, a line of fixed lights runs under the roof along the centreline.
interior_spaces.fixed_furniture: The cross benches, the folding rails hinged inside every opening, and, as a proposal, the bicycle racks at both ends.
interior_spaces.identity: Rows of benches running across the width between two long bands of glazed gates, so the whole room faces the pier side at every stop.
interior_spaces.undetermined: The foundation does not decide the standing capacity of the hall.

locations.story_use: The design treatment happens here: the team lays the ferry out as a strip of paper with card benches and slides the card helm cabin into place.
locations.layout: One long room with a single long table down its middle and a clear walkway around it on every side. Tall windows run along one long wall and a pinboard covers the wall opposite them.

a pinboard covering the wall opposite the windows

locations.name: The building dock
locations.description: A covered building dock where large vessels are framed under cover and floated out when they are finished.
locations.story_use: The construction, finishing and launch happen here: the framing for both ends is set out from one template, the sides rise as posts and openings, the gates are hung and the hull coated on its blocks, and in completion the dock is flooded and the finished ferry floats out through the gate.
locations.layout: One tall, long covered dock with a level floor below the level of the harbour outside. A watertight gate closes the harbour end, staging towers stand along both long walls, and crane rails run the length of the dock overhead.

connections.via: the dock gate at the harbour end, once the dock is flooded and the gate is open

fixed_features: a line of building blocks along the floor
staging towers along both long walls

flooding culverts along the dock floor
light_sources: a band of roof lights along the ridge
floodlights fixed to the staging towers

locations.name: The ferry's hall
locations.description: The covered passenger hall that fills the ferry's main deck from one end to the other.
locations.story_use: The crossing happens here: passengers board across the width and ride across the harbour beside the closed gates.
locations.layout: One long open space on the main deck under the roof, between the bulwarks at the two ends, its floor level from end to end and a short step above the pier. Its port and starboard sides are each a row of openings between posts, nothing divides it along its length, and the crew stair opens through it on the centreline at mid-length, rising to the hatch in the helm cabin floor and going down to the crew spaces in the hull.

the side openings along whichever side lies against the far pier

fixed_features: a row of openings between posts along the port side
a row of openings between posts along the starboard side
